name: Unknown BSC swap-bot contract lets anyone swap approved wallets without slippage limits
summary: Unverified contract 0x16d7c6f4, used by an operator's many EOAs to trade for managed wallets, exposes f8c03cc4(tokenIn, tokenOut, fee, amountIn, buyBack, 0, wallet). It pulls amountIn from any wallet that approved it and sells it on PancakeSwap V3 with no minimum output. It then buys the same amount back with the caller's tokens and sends it to the caller. There is no caller authorization. After draining the pool's other side, the attacker called it for 152 approved wallets in three transactions, receiving their TA, WBNB and USD1 for dust.
notes: Direct, immutable runtime (constructor immutables: owner 0x6d8bace1, router 0x13f4ea83). The unauthenticated, zero-minimum swap entry point exists from deployment. Wallet approvals only set exposure, and the owner's later calls only withdraw balances.

Gross debits of the 152 approved wallets named as the wallet argument in the three campaign transactions. The wallets received only dust back (24935602 wei USDT and 0.0083 TA in total), which is not netted. TA is illiquid, and the attacker's same-transaction sale moved its price, so TA is valued at realised proceeds: 282180.028682576245452554 USDT net to attacker contract 0x5b0d9b3c in source-1 (DefiLlama quoted 0.102143 before the sale). WBNB and USD1 are valued at DefiLlama quotes. Flash liquidity and the attacker's buy-back inputs are excluded.

The contract has no verified source. The missing caller check and zero minimum output are established from traces and calldata: attacker contracts created at blocks 55013996/55014240/55015921 were served, and the router calls carry amountOutMinimum 0. They are not established from source text.
